core.title: Derive feature names from produce/consume artifacts as {verb}-{domain|resource}
core.given: A feature produces/consumes artifacts (WHAT: entities, states, events); features are HOW (actions, capabilities).
core.when: You derive, add, rename or review the feature's name.
core.then: Name it {verb}-{domain} if it acts on the entire domain, {verb}-{resource} if on a specific resource within the domain; choose the verb by artifact type (event, state, data, config).
prefer: Typical verbs (not closed lists): events (past tense: ended, started, closed) → publish, emit, start, close, trigger; states (adjectives: remaining, active, current) → track, monitor, maintain, update; data (nouns: choice, identity, profile) → create, manage, process, handle, make; configs (config, settings, agreement) → configure, setup, initialize, define.
Another verb that fits better is fine, e.g. the verb form of the artifact (identity → identify-<domain>).
Identify domain and resource from the artifact's meaning; in a nested name the domain is not necessarily the part before the colon.
avoid: Naming the feature after the artifact (WHAT) instead of an action (HOW) on it.
A verb that does not fit the artifact's type and meaning.
Resource as object when the feature acts on the whole domain, or domain when it targets one resource.
core.why: A consistent WHAT→HOW transformation makes feature names derivable from artifacts so the plan stays coherent.
evidence: Each feature name is {verb}-{noun}, where the noun is the domain or the resource of one of its produce/consume artifacts.
The verb fits the artifact type (event/state/data/config) and meaning — a typical verb from that family or another appropriate verb.

The domain-vs-resource choice matches the feature's focus (whole domain vs specific resource), with domain/resource identified as the artifact's meaning indicates (not assumed to be the colon prefix).
verification: A check applies the two object rules: '{verb}-{domain}' when the domain is the primary focus of the feature (it acts on the entire domain), and '{verb}-{resource}' when the resource is the primary focus (it acts on a specific resource within the domain).

Verb lists are typical, not exhaustive: a check does not flag a verb solely for being outside the family list; a verb that fits the artifact's type and meaning (e.g. the artifact's own verb form) passes.
Domain and resource are identified from the artifact's meaning, not by position in a nested name; the per-family worked examples are reference examples, not a general parsing rule for nested names.
Verb selection depends on the event/state/data/config classification defined by the sibling naming-patterns convention for artifacts.

The reference realization ships no automated detector for this rule; artifact typing, domain-vs-resource focus and verb fit are semantic (llm_judged) findings established by review of the plan artifact.

fires: A feature is being named for an artifact it produces or consumes (event, state, data or config) in a plan artifact, planning doc or acceptance.
A feature is renamed or its name is reviewed against the artifacts it produces/consumes.
A new produce/consume artifact is introduced and the feature that works with it must be seeded.
doesNotFire: Naming the artifact itself (its domain:resource name) — governed by the naming-patterns convention.
Coder-side naming of functions, files or variables inside an implementation.
Editing a feature's acceptances or description without touching its name or artifacts.

neutralityNotes: This rule is a plan-level naming convention with almost no stack surface, so the core reproduces given/when/then/prefer/avoid/evidence/why essentially verbatim. The separators it uses — the hyphen in {verb}-{domain}/{verb}-{resource} and the colon in domain:resource artifact names — belong to the shared planning language defined by the sibling naming-patterns convention rather than to a runtime stack, so they are kept in the core text instead of being moved to a profile key. The only stack-local data are the plan-artifact kind names (wagon manifest, feature manifest), carried by roles.plan_artifact.kinds; the core activation uses neutral kind terms (plan artifact, planning doc, interface/artifact contract). The per-family worked examples, the sibling rule id plus its dependency-graph edge, and the activation-fact notes/audit/trace/additions bookkeeping are realization material and stay in bun.json, which is delivered as the worked reference example. Nothing required a new profile key.
